methodologyNotes: Covers manually-operated and motorized linear camera sliders (roughly 11-96in of advertised camera travel, handheld or tripod-mounted) that a video buyer cross-shops in 2026, spanning budget (Sevenoak, Neewer), prosumer (Zeapon, Konova, Rhino Camera Gear, Accsoon, iFootage), and professional/cinema gear (edelkrone, Syrp/Manfrotto, Kessler Crane, Proaim), plus the MOZA Slypod E monopod/slider hybrid. Excludes vehicle-mount rigs, pure jibs/cranes, and phone-only gimbal-sliders. rail_length_in is the manufacturer-advertised camera travel/sliding distance in inches; where a brand publishes both a physical rail length and a longer achieved-travel figure (e.g. edelkrone's tripod-doubling design, Zeapon's double-distance carriage), the marketed travel figure is used and the raw rail length is noted in provenance. max_payload_lb is the single headline payload figure a brand publishes for the product's primary orientation (horizontal slider travel for slider-first products; vertical support for the monopod-hybrid Slypod E); a second, different-orientation figure some brands also publish is noted in provenance rather than used as the primary number. motorized is true only when the specific SKU/base kit ships with an integrated motor; sliders that merely accept an optional add-on motor module (edelkrone, Konova, iFootage) are recorded false with the option noted in provenance. flywheel_drag is true only when the manufacturer's own material explicitly names a flywheel (or equivalent named damping wheel) as part of the base kit; ball-bearing tracks, friction knobs, and fluid-dampened carriages without an explicit flywheel claim are recorded false. mounting_thread is the camera/tripod thread size(s) as published or, for one product, as visually confirmed from a manufacturer product photo; null where no accessible source stated it. foldable is true only on an explicit folding/detachable-leg claim, and left null (not false) when a source is simply silent, since many bare-rail sliders without legs don't meaningfully have a fold state either way. incline_capable is true only on an explicit incline/angle/vertical-use claim (usually tied to independently adjustable legs); null otherwise. weight_lb is the slider unit's own weight (converted from kg where needed), excluding packaging. priceUsd is a US-market MSRP/starting price, recorded null rather than a foreign-currency conversion or an unverified reseller markdown wherever a clean current US figure could not be independently confirmed. Pricing/spec access was the dominant constraint on this category: edelkrone.com, konova.com, zeapon.com, ifootagegear.com, gvmled.com, kesslercrane.com, thegripstore.com, neewer.com, proaim.com/proaimusa.com, and every B&H/Adorama/Amazon/Walmart product page returned persistent HTTP 403/429/500 bot-blocking across many independently-timed attempts; specs and pricing were instead sourced from manuals-aggregator sites (search-manual.com, manualslib.com), authorized resellers (marcotec-shop, studio-supplies, proavsupplies, wexphotovideo, pitbullaudio), manufacturer pages that did load (accsoon.com, manfrotto.com), and editorial reviews (CineD, Fstoppers, Digital Camera World's 2026 buying guide, which independently corroborated several picks), each cited per product. Two seed products were investigated and dropped rather than published with fabricated data: GVM's GR-80QD storefront was unreachable on every attempt with no independent source yielding verifiable specs, and the originally-seeded 'SmallRig 24-inch' slider turned out on verification to be the SmallRig MS-10 (39in, discontinued, explicitly 'Not for sale in the U.S. and Canada') and was excluded as not a 2026 US-buyer-comparable product; Accsoon TopRig S60 and Proaim SL-303 were added in their place after independent corroboration (a 2026 Digital Camera World buying guide independently named the Neewer ER1, edelkrone SliderPLUS PRO Long, and Rhino ROV as category leaders, validating those seed picks; it also surfaced Accsoon TopRig S60 as a notable 2026 pick). Images: Wikimedia Commons used where a genuine, brand-matching photo existed (2 of 12, both visually verified); otherwise a directly-fetched and visually-verified manufacturer or authorized-reseller product photo; omitted entirely (not null) for the 3 products where no accessible, verifiably-matching image could be found — for Proaim specifically, a candidate image was found but rejected after visual inspection because it depicted a different Proaim product line ('Velvet') rather than the SL-303. All sources accessed 2026-08-01.

products.name: edelkrone SliderPLUS PRO (Long)
products.priceNote: edelkrone.com returned HTTP 429 on every direct attempt, so no clean current US MSRP could be independently confirmed. German reseller Marcotec lists a discounted price of EUR288.94 against a EUR824.05 strike-through 'was' price for the Compact size, which is not treated as a reliable US MSRP given currency/VAT differences and the possibility of an inflated compare-at price, so priceUsd is left null rather than converted or guessed.

specs.mounting_thread: 3/8"-16 (top camera stud and bottom mounting port)

products.provenance: edelkrone's own site was unreachable (429) on repeated attempts, so specs come from Marcotec's German storefront listing, which documents both the Compact (50cm/19.7in tripod travel, 25lb/11.3kg payload, 3.41lb/1.55kg) and Long (90cm/35.4in tripod travel, 20lb/9kg payload, 4.05lb/1.84kg) size variants of the v5 PRO generation; Long is recorded here as it is the size a 2026 Digital Camera World buying guide specifically names ('Edelkrone SliderPLUS v5 PRO Long' - 'Best premium slider'). Both variants share: non-friction ball-bearing tracking system (no flywheel), 3/8"-16 mounting on top and bottom, and built-in legs each independently adjustable for uneven terrain/inclines. A secondary listing from rental house Bolt Productions, describing what it calls the 'SliderPLUS Pro Large' (27.6in sliding range, 15-26lb capacity depending on section of the page, CNC aluminum, steel ball bearings, single 3/8" mounting hole), corroborates the general construction and mounting but uses different length/payload figures under a different size name, which is flagged here as likely reflecting a different generation/size-naming convention rather than being folded into the primary Long spec. Motorization is available only via edelkrone's separately-sold Motor Module, so the base kit is recorded non-motorized. No image could be sourced from either retailer page (both returned binary/blocked responses when an image URL was requested), so a Wikimedia Commons photo of the SliderPLUS PRO with an FS700 camera mounted (uploaded by Enginsula, CC BY-SA 4.0) is used instead after visual confirmation it depicts the correct slider family.

products.name: Rhino Camera Gear ROV PRO Traveler (16")
products.priceNote: Reseller ExposureNest lists this unit at a $148.00 sale price against a $315.00 strike-through 'was' price; $148 is used here as the concretely-observed transactable figure since the $315 comparison price could not be independently verified as a genuine former MSRP (Rhino's own site was not reachable to confirm).
products.provenance: Specs from authorized reseller ExposureNest's product listing for the ROV PRO Traveler: 25in/63.5cm physical track producing a 16in/40.64cm camera travel distance (the 16 in the product name refers to travel, not overall track length, and is used as rail_length_in per this dataset's convention), 5lb/2.27kg max payload, slider-only weight 1.4lb/0.64kg (5.4lb boxed), folding all-terrain legs, and a self-contained motor with belt-tension adjustable via a 1.5mm Allen key rather than a friction/flywheel knob. A 2026 Digital Camera World buying guide independently names the Rhino ROV line ('Perfect for YouTubers') as a current category pick, corroborating this remains a notable 2026 product. Incline capability is not explicitly documented by the reseller so is left null despite the all-terrain legs (which primarily address uneven ground leveling, not necessarily active incline shooting). Image is a Wikimedia Commons photo of this exact model (CC BY 2.0, Tony Webster/Flickr), found via Commons media search and confirmed to show the ROV PRO Traveler.

products.name: Zeapon Micro 2 Plus
products.priceNote: zeapon.com and every retailer product page attempted (B&H, Pergear, IndiProTools) returned 403/404/429 blocks. A Fstoppers review's comment section cited roughly $285 for the slider plus $225 for the separate motor module ($510 total) from a B&H listing, but this is an unverified third-party recollection rather than a page this dataset directly confirmed, so priceUsd is left null.
products.provenance: Zeapon's own storefront and every retailer page attempted returned bot-blocks, so specs come from Fstoppers' hands-on review: physical rail approximately 13in/35cm producing an approximately 22in/56cm double-distance travel (the 22in figure is used as rail_length_in per this dataset's travel-distance convention), 4.5kg/9.9lb max payload, 1.8kg/4.0lb slider weight, a built-in foldable stand, a 'fluid dampening rail' (recorded as flywheel_drag: false since the review's own wording names fluid dampening rather than a flywheel), and confirmed smooth performance across various mounting angles including vertical. Motorized electronic operation with Sony NP-F battery power and three adjustable speeds plus smartphone app control. Image is the review's lead photo, a close-up clearly showing 'Micro 2 Plus' branding on the unit, verified by direct visual inspection; used under an editorial/press-photo basis attributed to Zeapon as manufacturer.

products.name: MOZA Slypod E
products.priceNote: Launch MSRP per CineD's specs/price article; this has remained the standard listed price at MOZA-authorized retailers.
products.provenance: CineD's launch article (December 2019, $299 price confirmed at time of writing and still the standard MOZA price today) documents the Slypod E as a motorized monopod/slider hybrid: 11in/280mm travel distance, aluminum-alloy construction (vs. the original Slypod's carbon fiber), 9kg/19.8lb vertical (monopod) load rating recorded here as the primary payload since vertical monopod use is the product's core use case, with a separate, lower 4kg/8.8lb rating for horizontal/sliding use noted for buyers comparing it against dedicated sliders. Weight 2.02lb/920g. Ten-speed button control plus smartphone app, USB-C rechargeable with roughly 2 hours of runtime. 'Foldable' does not clearly apply to this telescoping-monopod form factor and is left null rather than asserted either way; incline_capable is true since operating at any angle from horizontal to vertical is the product's defining feature. Image is the article's featured photo showing the actual device (verified by direct visual inspection).

products.name: Neewer 47.2" Carbon Fiber Camera Slider
products.priceNote: neewer.com and Best Buy's product page could not be loaded (429 / repeated timeout) to confirm a current US price; the reseller page used for specs does not display one, so priceUsd is left null.
products.provenance: This is Neewer's manual (non-motorized) 47.2in/120cm carbon fiber slider (model 131027), matching the original 'Neewer 47-inch Carbon' seed more closely than Neewer's separate motorized ER1 model (which a 2026 Digital Camera World buying guide names 'Best slider overall' but for which no independently-fetchable spec page could be reached). Confirmed specs: 47.2in/120cm rail, 17.5lb/8kg max payload, six U-shaped ball bearings for the drag mechanism (no flywheel), 5.69lb weight, foldable/compact carrying design with included bag, and support for vertical, horizontal, and 45-degree shooting angles. Mounting thread size was not stated on the reseller page and is left null. Image is the primary product photo on the reseller page, clearly showing 'NEEWER' branding and matching the described carbon-fiber rail with gold-accented hardware, confirmed by direct visual inspection.

products.name: Konova K5-150 Slider (150cm)
products.priceNote: konova.com and konovaphoto.com both returned 429 on every attempt, and Amazon/B&H product pages could not be loaded, so no current US price could be independently confirmed.
products.provenance: Konova's own site was unreachable (429) on every attempt, so the mechanism/mounting/leg details come from a Konova K5 user manual hosted on search-manual.com, which documents the shared K5-series hardware: 8mm chrome-plated steel rails on three steel bearings, a friction-adjustment knob (not a flywheel by default -- Konova sells a 'Nitsan Fly Wheel' as a separate accessory for the K5, confirming a flywheel is available but not standard), 3/8"-16 camera thread, 1/4"-20 plus 3/8"-16 tripod threads, and detachable, height/angle-adjustable legs. The 59.1in/150cm length and 55lb/25kg payload figures are specific to the K5-150 size and are taken from an Amazon US listing title ('Konova Slider K5 150 (59.1 inch) ... Payloads up to 55bs (25kg)') surfaced via search, since Amazon's product page itself returned a server error on direct fetch; the manual's own worked example covers the shorter K5-60 (23.6in, ~50.7-55lb) size, whose payload figure is consistent with the K5-150 listing and supports treating 55lb as accurate across this series. Weight was not found for the 150cm size specifically and is left null rather than extrapolated. Image is a Konova-branded product photo hosted alongside the manual, confirmed by direct visual inspection to show a Konova slider with visible branding.

products.name: iFootage Shark Slider S1
products.priceNote: iFootage's EU storefront lists the Standard bundle at EUR449.90; no comparable US-specific price page could be reached (ifootagegear.com's US site and B&H/Adorama listings all returned bot-blocks), so priceUsd is left null rather than converting the EU figure.
products.provenance: A user-manual excerpt indexed by search-manual.com describes the S1's carriage as riding on 'long-lasting silent bearings imported from Japan, synchronous belts, and a flywheel' supporting up to 15lb across a 25in sliding distance -- the explicit flywheel naming is why flywheel_drag is recorded true here (unlike several other products in this dataset that only have ball bearings or friction knobs). iFootage's EU site separately confirms the product is sold as a modular, tool-less, belt-driven slider with an optional motion-control kit (S1A1S) available, so the base kit is recorded non-motorized. Mounting thread, foldability, and incline capability were not stated in either accessible source and are left null. No usable image could be sourced: the EU product page did not expose a static image URL in its fetched markup, and other retailer pages (goodcameraequipment.com, digitalzakka.com, hashmiphotos.com, aabworld.com) all returned 403 responses, so the image key is omitted entirely per this dataset's rule against guessing an image URL.

products.name: Syrp Magic Carpet PRO Medium Slider (91cm)
products.priceNote: Manfrotto's own product page (Syrp's parent brand) does not display a price, and other retailer pages attempted (Filmtools, AVGear, B&H) returned parse errors or 429 blocks, so priceUsd is left null.

specs.mounting_thread: 3/8"-16 and 1/4"-20 (female, tripod end); 1/4"-20 and 3/8"-16 (male, camera end)

products.provenance: Manfrotto (which acquired Syrp) lists the Magic Carpet PRO Medium at 91cm/35.8in of travel, a 32kg/70.5lb tracking-movement payload rating, 'press button engagement of motion smoothing flywheel' (an explicit flywheel claim, hence flywheel_drag: true), 3/8"-16 and 1/4"-20 threads on both the tripod and camera ends, aluminum construction, and a 5.7kg/12.6lb weight. The product is Syrp motion-control compatible (accepts a separate motorized Genie unit) but ships manual, so motorized is recorded false. Foldability and incline capability were not addressed on the product page and are left null -- this is a bare track system without integrated legs of its own. Image is Manfrotto's own CDN-hosted product photo, confirmed by direct visual inspection to show a slider bearing visible 'Syrp' branding.

products.name: Kessler CineSlider
products.priceNote: kesslercrane.com returned 429 on every attempt; Markertek's listing for this model states 'This item is no longer available' with no price shown, so priceUsd is left null.
products.provenance: Kessler's own site could not be reached (429 on every attempt across the session), so specs come from two resellers whose listings agree closely: ProAVSupplies and Markertek both describe this 3ft-class CineSlider as offering 35.5in of camera travel, supporting camera rigs up to 80lb, weighing only 10lb, measuring 40.5in x 5in, with 'drag control and locking' for the manual handle (not explicitly named a flywheel, so flywheel_drag is left null rather than asserted true or false), a standard 3/8" mounting bolt plus an optional 100mm bowl adapter, and compatibility with tripod, fluid-head, and light-stand mounting configurations plus Kessler's motion-control systems. B&H search snippets separately reference other CineSlider lengths (a 60.5in/80lb 'no crank' model and a 28.5in/7.7lb 'Traveler' model), confirming this is a multi-size product line, but this entry specifically documents the 3ft/35.5in configuration both resellers describe. Foldability and incline capability were not stated by either source and are left null. No usable product image could be sourced -- proavsupplies.com's image request was blocked (429) and Kessler's own site was unreachable -- so the image key is omitted entirely.

products.name: Sevenoak SK-TXS80 Carbon Fibre Slider (80cm)
products.priceNote: Wex Photo Video (UK) lists this at GBP379.99; no US retailer page (Adorama returned 403) could be reached to confirm a US-specific price, so priceUsd is left null rather than converted from GBP.
products.provenance: UK retailer Wex Photo Video's listing (product ID 1612410, matching the URL slug exactly) describes this as an 82cm overall-length unit marketed as an '80cm' slider (the 80cm/31.5in nominal figure is used as rail_length_in, consistent with how the product is named and sold), supporting camera weights up to 10kg/22lb, with a 'belt driven system with smooth flywheel function' (explicit flywheel claim), 1/4" and 3/8" threads on the sliding plate plus a standard 3/8" tripod fitting, angle-adjustable legs with height-adjustable rubber feet and a built-in spirit level (supporting incline_capable: true), carbon-fiber construction, and an included carry case. Weight and foldability were not stated on the page and are left null. Adorama's US listing for a related Sevenoak model (SK-LS85, a different 85cm/33.46in SKU) could not be fetched (403) so was not used for this entry. Image is Wex's own product photo for this exact listing ID, showing a black carbon-fiber-look track slider with red rubber feet consistent with the description.

products.name: Accsoon TopRig S60
products.priceNote: Original US MSRP of $399 per Accsoon's own US reseller page; the same page shows a current price of $419, so $399 is used here as the manufacturer-stated starting/launch price.

specs.mounting_thread: 1/4"-20 (visually confirmed camera-mount stud in product photo)

products.provenance: Accsoon's official spec page confirms the S60 (distinct from the shorter S40) offers 425mm/16.7in of travel, a 4.0kg/8.8lb horizontal load rating (used here as the primary payload figure since horizontal/slider use is this product's main use case) against a lower 2.5kg/5.5lb vertical rating, a 1.5kg/3.3lb unit weight, fixed dimensions of 610x106x71.3mm, and a brushless-motor drive with no mention of a flywheel (hence flywheel_drag: false). Accsoon's US reseller page corroborates an $8.8lb-class payload, states an original $399 MSRP against a current $419 price, and adds Bluetooth app control, an onboard button/speed-knob panel, 120-degree pan, A/B point time-lapse, and NP-F/USB-C/DC power options. The product photo (bigcommerce-hosted on Accsoon's own US storefront) shows a single rigid rail with small fixed rubber feet and no leg hinges, which is the basis for recording foldable: false and for confirming a 1/4"-20 camera-mount stud visible on the carriage (mounting_thread recorded as visually confirmed rather than from text, since neither source's text stated a thread size). Incline capability was not addressed by either source and is left null. This is a 2026-current pick per a Digital Camera World buying guide ('Best with built-in controller').

products.name: Proaim SL-303 Professional 8ft Video Camera Slider
products.priceNote: proaim.com, proaimusa.com, and B&H's product page all returned HTTP 429/403 on every attempt, so no current US price could be independently confirmed via a directly-fetched page.
products.provenance: Proaim's own product pages and B&H's listing both returned persistent bot-blocks (429/403) across every attempt this session, so the mounting/hardware details come from the SL-303's assembly manual hosted on ManualsLib, which confirms an 8ft/96in slider with 100mm bowl mounting (75mm conversion ring included), 4 Allen keys, 8 leveling feet, 4 end feet, and 3 mounting knobs in the box, plus toolless assembly. The 33lb payload figure was visible in Proaim's own product-page meta-description as surfaced through a search-engine results page (proaim.com/proaimusa.com's live pages themselves returned 429 on direct fetch, so this figure is corroborated only indirectly rather than via a page this dataset directly rendered). Weight, foldability, incline capability, and drag mechanism were not available in the accessible manual excerpt and are left null. A candidate product image found via ManualsLib was fetched, visually inspected, and rejected: it clearly showed a slider branded 'PROAIM VELVET' -- a different Proaim product line -- rather than the SL-303, so per this dataset's rule against using a mismatched image, the image key is omitted entirely for this product.
